traceability.evidence:
1) Config presets implemented and exported: - src/index.ts defines TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and createTraceabilityFlatConfig(), then: const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], }; - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts verifies: - default export includes rules and configs (plugin.configs === configs). - rules has the expected rule names (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference). - configs.recommended[0].rules contains the correct rule keys and severities. - configs.strict[0].rules equals configs.recommended[0].rules.
2) ESLint v9 flat config and project integration: - eslint.config.js is a flat config array (no .eslintrc) and is directly annotated for this story: /** * ESLint flat config for Traceability Plugin * @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md * @req REQ-FLAT-CONFIG - Setup ESLint v9 flat config for plugin usage */ - It uses js.configs.recommended from "@eslint/js" and file-based overrides for: - Node config files (CommonJS env/globals). - TypeScript files (parser: @typescript-eslint/parser with project/tsconfigRootDir). - JavaScript files. - Test files (Jest globals, relaxed complexity/max-lines). - A final ignores block for lib, node_modules, coverage, docs, *.md, etc. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts runs ESLint via its CLI using: --no-config-lookup --config eslint.config.js --stdin --rule ..., confirming the plugin works with this flat config in practice.
3) Rule options and JSON Schema validation (REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION): - require-story-annotation: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts defines meta.schema as: schema: [{ type: "object", properties: { scope: { type: "array", items: { type: "string", enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE }, uniqueItems: true }, exportPriority: { type: "string", enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES } }, additionalProperties: false }]. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts (/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */) asserts schema.properties.scope, schema.properties.exportPriority, and schema.additionalProperties === false. - valid-story-reference: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts meta.schema[0] defines options: storyDirectories (array of strings), allowAbsolutePaths (boolean), requireStoryExtension (boolean), with additionalProperties: false. - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts (/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */) checks these properties exist and that additionalProperties is false. - valid-annotation-format: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts builds a JSON schema in getRuleSchema() with nested story/req objects and flat shorthand fields, all under additionalProperties: false. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts uses that schema in meta.schema and performs runtime validation: resolveOptions() + getOptionErrors(). - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts includes many cases where invalid regex options (nested story.pattern/req.pattern and flat storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) produce messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration" with stable error text and the rule still runs using defaults. - require-branch-annotation + src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts validate branchTypes; on invalid values, validateBranchTypes() returns a Program listener that reports configuration errors like: Value "UnknownType" should be equal to one of the allowed values: IfStatement, SwitchCase, ...; this is asserted in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts.
4) Customizable story paths and directories (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS) and rule options (REQ-RULE-OPTIONS): - valid-annotation-format: - Options shape (AnnotationRuleOptions) supports nested story.pattern/example and req.pattern/example plus flat storyPathPattern/storyPathExample/requirementIdPattern/requirementIdExample, resolved by resolveOptions(). - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts verify: - Custom patterns/examples for story and req (nested and flat). - Precedence of nested options over flat. - Error text includes the configured example values. - Invalid regex patterns are reported and safely ignored (fallback to defaults). - valid-story-reference: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts uses defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"] and options storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension. - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts covers: - Custom storyDirectories resolving relative paths like "// @story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md". - allowAbsolutePaths true/false behavior for absolute paths inside project. - requireStoryExtension false allowing .md paths when storyDirectories point to existing files. - Project boundary and misconfigured storyDirectories outside the project root still causing invalidPath diagnostics, not false positives.
5) Documentation, user experience, and troubleshooting (User Experience, Documentation, REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION): - README.md: - Shows flat-config usage with: import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability"; export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended]; - Provides an example flat config that directly wires plugin rules (plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { "traceability/require-story-annotation": "error", ... }). - Links to user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, user-docs/api-reference.md, user-docs/examples.md, user-docs/migration-guide.md, and docs/config-presets.md. - docs/config-presets.md describes the built-in recommended and strict presets, lists the exact rules and severities, and gives flat-config code examples combining js.configs.recommended with traceability.configs.recommended/strict. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md (flat config focused) includes: - Quick Setup, JavaScript-only, TypeScript, mixed JS/TS, test file, and monorepo flat-config patterns. - A dedicated section on enabling the traceability plugin via traceability.configs.recommended. - A Troubleshooting ESLint Configuration section addressing common misconfigurations (parser, deprecated flags, globals, etc.). - user-docs/api-reference.md documents rule options in detail and includes a "Configuration Presets" section with example flat configs using traceability.configs.recommended and traceability.configs.strict. - user-docs/examples.md provides runnable flat-config examples using both recommended and strict presets. - user-docs/migration-guide.md explains configuration changes when moving to v1.x and how to load traceability.configs.recommended in eslint.config.js.
6) Direct traceability to Story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG and its requirements: - Story file exists: docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md (4099 bytes) with the listed acceptance criteria and requirements. - eslint.config.js includes @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md and @req REQ-FLAT-CONFIG. - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts and tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts both have a file-level /** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */ and test names referencing [REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] and [REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION]. - The existence of these tests, plus the structural tests in plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts, shows that configuration loading, validation, and rule application are all covered by automated tests.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements for docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md are implemented and backed by concrete code, tests, and documentation.
- Core Functionality / REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS: The plugin exports recommended and strict presets via src/index.ts (configs.recommended and configs.strict). Their contents and severities are validated by tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts and described in docs/config-presets.md and user-docs/api-reference.md. - Quality Standards / REQ-FLAT-CONFIG: The project uses ESLint v9 flat configuration exclusively (eslint.config.js), annotated as implementing REQ-FLAT-CONFIG. The config follows ESLint 9 best practices (array of configs, js.configs.recommended, languageOptions, ignores, no extends) and is exercised by cli-integration Jest tests and documented in user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md. - Integration / REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION: Example configs in README.md, user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, user-docs/examples.md, and user-docs/migration-guide.md cover JavaScript, TypeScript, mixed projects, monorepos, config files, and test files. tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts proves the plugin works end-to-end with ESLint CLI and the flat config. - User Experience & Documentation: There is comprehensive user-facing documentation covering installation, flat-config setup, presets, per-rule options, examples, migration, and troubleshooting. These directly address setup for common project types and error scenarios. - Error Handling / REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION & REQ-RULE-OPTIONS: Rule configurations are described with explicit JSON Schemas (additionalProperties: false) and runtime validation. Invalid configuration values (e.g., bad regex patterns, invalid branchTypes) are caught and surfaced as clear ESLint diagnostics (invalidRuleConfiguration, explicit error messages), while the rules fall back to safe defaults. This is well covered by tests in tests/config/*.test.ts and tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts and tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts.
Based on this evidence, the ESLint configuration setup story (002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG) is fully implemented, with passing tests and thorough documentation.
